page:
- Server-Timing Middleware: adds performance metrics to response headers via the Server-Timing header
- Note: on Cloudflare Workers, timer metrics may be inaccurate since timers only show the time of the last I/O
- Import: `import { Hono } from 'hono'`, `import { timing, setMetric, startTime, endTime, wrapTime } from 'hono/timing'`, `import type { TimingVariables } from 'hono/timing'`
- Usage: `app.use(timing())`; custom metrics via `setMetric(c, 'region', 'europe-west3')` or with timing `setMetric(c, 'custom', 23.8, 'My custom Metric')`; timers via `startTime(c, 'db')` / `endTime(c, 'db')`, or wrap a promise with `wrapTime(c, 'db', promise)`
- Conditionally enable timing per request via the `enabled` option function, e.g. only for POST requests
- Options: `total` (boolean, default `true`), `enabled` (boolean or function, default `true`), `totalDescription` (string, default `Total Response Time`), `autoEnd` (boolean, controls whether `startTime()` ends automatically at request end), `crossOrigin` (boolean/string/function, default `false`, controls which origins can read the timing header)
- Questions answered: How do I add Server-Timing headers in Hono? How do I add custom timing metrics? How do I disable timing for certain requests? Why are Cloudflare Workers timer metrics inaccurate? How do I allow cross-origin access to timing headers?

sections.manifest:
- Import statements for Server-Timing Middleware
- `import { Hono } from 'hono'`
- `import { timing, setMetric, startTime, endTime, wrapTime } from 'hono/timing'`
- `import type { TimingVariables } from 'hono/timing'`
- Answers: How do I import the Server-Timing Middleware and its helper functions?

- Specify `type Variables = TimingVariables` and `new Hono<{ Variables: Variables }>()` to type `c.get('metric')`
- Register with `app.use(timing())`
- `setMetric(c, 'region', 'europe-west3')` adds a custom metric without timing
- `setMetric(c, 'custom', 23.8, 'My custom Metric')` adds a custom metric with a timing value (in milliseconds) and description
- `startTime(c, 'db')` starts a named timer; `endTime(c, 'db')` ends it
- `wrapTime(c, 'db', db.findMany(...))` wraps a Promise to time it automatically
- Conditionally enabled example: `timing({ enabled: (c) => c.req.method === 'POST' })` applied with `app.use('*', ...)`
- Answers: How do I add a custom named timer? How do I record a custom metric with a value and description? How do I wrap a promise to time it? How do I only enable timing for POST requests?

- Shows an example screenshot (`/images/timing-example.png`) of the Server-Timing output as seen in browser devtools
- Answers: What does the Server-Timing Middleware output look like?

- `total`: `boolean`, optional, default `true` — show the total response time
- `enabled`: `boolean | (c: Context) => boolean`, optional, default `true` — whether timings are added to headers
- `totalDescription`: `string`, optional, default `Total Response Time` — description for the total response time metric
- `autoEnd`: `boolean`, optional — whether `startTime()` should end automatically at the end of the request; if disabled, timers not manually ended are not shown
- `crossOrigin`: `boolean | string | (c: Context) => boolean | string`, optional, default `false` — controls which origins can read the Timing-Allow-Origin header; `false` restricts to the current origin, `true` allows all origins, a string (comma-separated for multiple) allows specific domains
- Answers: What is the default value of the `total` option? How do I set a custom description for total response time? What happens if autoEnd is disabled? How do I allow another domain to read Server-Timing headers via Timing-Allow-Origin?
